classes.name: Oral corticosteroids
classes.description: Systemic oral corticosteroids: prednisone (tablets, solution; Rayos delayed-release appears discontinued), methylprednisolone (Medrol, dose pack), prednisolone (solution, Orapred ODT, Millipred), dexamethasone (tablets, solution, Dexamethasone Intensol, TaperDex/Dxevo/HiDex packs; Hemady 20 mg is labeled for multiple myeloma only, an alternative, never the pick), hydrocortisone (Cortef; Alkindi Sprinkle and Khindivi oral solution for children). Deflazacort (Emflaza) and vamorolone (Agamree) for Duchenne are specialty alternatives only, never the pick. Not budesonide (Entocort, Uceris, Tarpeyo) or inhaled/topical steroids.
classes.plainDescription: Short courses of steroid pills that calm inflammation fast, for flares of asthma, COPD, arthritis, allergies and more.
classes.indication: Inflammatory flares, asthma/COPD exacerbations, autoimmune disease, adrenal insufficiency

records.verificationNote: Read from the formulary text layer, row by row (each tier digit sits on the same row as its drug name; pypdf gave no x-coordinates for the digits). Formulary sig and quantity limits are as printed; the document prints no sig, so the sig is the label starting dose. Prednisone 10 mg tablet is Tier 1 with no PA; BvsD is a Part B versus Part D review flag, not a PA, so it is not in preferredRestriction (PDG p. 61). Not listed: Rayos, Medrol, Orapred ODT, Millipred, Cortef, TaperDex, Dxevo, HiDex. Hydrocortisone tablets print on p. 54 (in the list's dermatology block) and are cited as printed. [Sonnet check 2026-11-06: tiers and flags re-read in layout (row-aligned) extraction, not flattened text; nonformulary reasons reworded to the front-matter wording; prednisone tablets carry BvsD (Part B vs D review, not PA); dose pack does not; added Rayos and Khindivi as not listed.] [Reused: same national Humana Premier Rx PDP]
